scope: Independent source and existing offline-evidence review only
conclusions: Native response cookie headers are retained immediately after route.fetch, before body/status/size refusal; observed nonempty cookies remain available for independent cleanup.
Only helper import wiring and native cookie-header ordering changed; strict source/live/asset/request/authority/data/privacy/dispatch guards remain intact.
Shared imports and copied tests use the coherent canonical-v3 helper set; its separate canonical-source review and committed-source preflight remain applicable.
limitations: This review performs no auth, network, browser, job, SQL or staging execution and grants no live acceptance.
Actual selectors, public representations, pixels, session cleanup and parent acceptance still require a separately reviewed concrete plan and observed execution.

Unexpected new cookie issuance while closing an extra-cookie temporary subject remains a fail-latched robustness limitation; released sign-out only expires cookies and native GETs do not issue sessions, so it is not a demonstrated released-source blocker.
